Reason for rejecting the above arguments 19.
The reason for rejecting the above argument ensues from a reading of the signatured disclosure statement of convict Balbir Singh.
The said signatured disclosure statement occurs in Ex. P-28.
The said exhibit has been drawn on 14.5.2016.

Therefore, given its being drawn on the said date,
CRA-D-885-2019 (O&M) and other connected cases -12- which is but prior to the convict (supra)
becoming committed to judicial custody, thus it cannot be said, that it was not made by convict Balbir Singh during the phase of his being in police custody, but was made by him when, as such he became put to judicial custody.

Moreover, in the confession of guilt borne in Ex. P-28, thereins occur recitals about convict Balbir Singh, using a knife in his committing the alleged offence, and,
his concealing the said knife near the outer wall of the house of his son Narinder Singh near Saidkheri underneath the earth.
The place of its hiding, and, keeping, is stated thereins to be known only to him.
Since through recovery memo Ex. P-29, he caused recovery of the incriminatory knife.
Therefore, the confession of guilt, as made in Ex. P-28, is not a bald and simpliciter confession, to which the embargo of Section 25 of the Indian Evidence Act, becomes invited.

Contrarily when in pursuance to its making, the convict (supra), through Ex. P-29 thus caused the recovery of the incriminatory knife, resultantly the confession of guilt Ex. P-28, becomes both admissible as well as a relevant piece of incriminatory evidence, thus against convict Balbir Singh.
20. Significantly also, when the weapon of offence was recovered from the place known only to the convict (supra).

Therefore, it cannot be said, that the recovery of the said weapon of offence, through Ex. P-29, is an engineered or a contrived recovery, which otherwise it could be so construed, if it was recovered from an open accessible place.
Since it was recovered from a secluded, and/or, a place which was known only to the accused concerned, therefore both Ex. P-28 and Ex. P-29 acquire evidentary worth.

21. Moreover, the fact of both the above exhibits thus carrying the signatures of convict Balbir Singh,
which however he neither denied nor the CRA-D-885-2019 (O&M) and other connected cases -13- said denial became ably proven by him, through his leading able evidence, resultantly both the above exhibits acquire formidable evidentary worth.
